findings.evidence: grep: `resolve_deps.py:89 TOOLCHAIN_RE = re.compile(r"leanprover/lean4:v(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)(?:-rc(\d+))?")`; `toolchain_tags.py:104 ... int(rc) if rc is not None else math.inf`; `check-bump.sh:193 ... int(rc) if rc is not None else float("inf")  # release > any rc`.
findings.fix: Extract the parse-and-order rule into one small stdlib-only module (e.g. `scripts/lean_versions.py`; it cannot be imported from `toolchain_tags.py`, which pulls in `zulip`/`lake_cache_probe` at import time) and have `resolve_deps.py`, `toolchain_tags.py` and `check-bump.sh`'s inline python all use it.
findings.issue: `TOOLCHAIN_RE`/`parse_toolchain` (lines 89, 224-230) is a third copy of the same rule: `toolchain_tags.py:90,96-104` (`RELEASE_RE`, `parse_release`, rc-less = inf) and the inline parser in `check-bump.sh:190-193`. The resolver's choice has to be accepted by the guard's `p < b` check, so the two must agree on what a forward toolchain move is; three independent regexes can drift (nightlies, extra suffixes) and make the resolver propose sets the guard rejects.

findings.evidence: resolve_deps.py:157 `...runs?branch=master&event=push...`; :168 `r["event"] == "push" and r["head_branch"] == "master"`; vs :333 `self.src.compare(self.mathlib_repo, m, self.mathlib_branch)` and :414 `branches = {MATHLIB: self.mathlib_branch}` used in the hold text at :442.
findings.fix: Pick one level: either thread the nominated branch through `cached_master_tip(repo, branch)`/`cache_published(..., branch)`, or drop the parameterization and assert `self.mathlib_branch == "master"` in `Resolver.__init__`, so the branch cannot silently mean two different things.
findings.issue: `mathlib_branch` is read from `lakefile.toml` and used for forwardness (`:333`) and for the hold text (`:414`, "N commits behind its newest cached <branch> commit"), but the cache queries ignore it: `cached_master_tip` hard-codes `branch=master&event=push` (:157) and `cache_published` requires `head_branch == "master"` (:168). The parameter never specializes to anything but `master` (CLAUDE.md: mathlib's `rev` must always remain `master`), so the generality is unused where it matters and the summary would report lag against the wrong branch if it were ever used.

summary: The resolver adds a third private copy of the Lean toolchain version/order rule that `toolchain_tags.py` and `check-bump.sh` already implement, and its `mathlib_branch` parameter is only half honoured — the cache queries hard-code `master`. Both should be settled at one level rather than per call site.
